Our Mission & Lived Experience

Hi, I am Jason. As a former Centre for Deaf and Hard of Hearing People (CfD) specialist and lifelong hearing loss initiate, I understand firsthand the barriers, communication fatigue, frustration, and isolation that can accompany hearing loss in daily life.

I founded the Hearing Loss Initiative to build the bridge that was missing in Bristol: connecting NHS clinical care with practical real-world support, verified assistive listening technology (including Bluetooth Auracast), acoustic venue auditing, and welcoming peer connection.

👂 Lived Experience First

Every guide, checklist, and roadmap is shaped by authentic lived experience with digital hearing aids, lipreading, and listening strain.

🏛️ Bristol-Wide Access

Auditing local venues & assessments (coming soon), verifying hearing loops, and championing quiet acoustics across the city.

🤝 Peer Connection & Support

Providing peer support, meetups (coming soon), and warm spaces where nobody has to struggle or nod along in silence.

💡 Practical Education

Equipping employers, families, and venues with the practical PACE communication framework and awareness workshops (coming soon).

🚀 Help Evolve the Initiative

Looking for Collaborators & Co-Founders

The Bristol Hearing Loss Initiative is evolving from an initial grassroots prototype into a comprehensive city-wide platform. As we scale into in-person workshops, venue accreditations, and funding partnerships, Founder Jason is actively looking for passionate people to join and help shape the next stage:

🤝 Co-Founders & OperationsPartners passionate about non-profit scaling, grant funding, and network partnerships.
💻 Technical & Design LeadsDevelopers, UI/UX designers, and audio tech testers eager to build innovative accessibility tools.
☕ Peer & Event HostsHard-of-hearing advocates to facilitate local peer groups and coffee meetups across Bristol.
🏛️ Venue & Business LiaisonsAmbassadors to connect with Bristol venues, employers, and NHS clinics for accessibility audits.

Our Immediate Priority: Evening Support Meetups

We are testing local demand for a free, regular Bristol evening support group. We want to bring adults with hearing loss together in quiet, accessible spaces with working loop systems to share experiences and practical coping strategies.

Once our initiate base grows, we intend to register as a Community Interest Company (CIC) to open doors for formal funding, initiative grants, and broader accessibility training programmes across Bristol.
